style: Nilachala style with a banded sixteen-sided dome on older stone masonry
key_structures: West-facing apsidal Natmandir with an elephant-back roof
Octagonal Manobhava Guha beneath the Vimana
Saubhagya and Rinmoksha Kund within the temple compound
special_features: Sacred spring-fed rock depression in the Manobhava Guha
Sacred stones for Matangi and Kamala in the same lower chamber
The survey places the cave floor 2.5 metres below the halls
Sculptured stone niches beneath the later brick dome
materials: Earlier stone foundation and sculpted granite
Banded brick shikhara and terracotta roofs
period: Early stone fabric, Koch rebuilding and Ahom additions
renovation_history: The temple authority records rebuilding in 1565 under the Koch rulers. The field survey documents the Natmandir dedication of 1759 under Rajeswar Singha.
